turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the device physics

**What the training set says wins (≥19–23 %):**
- **Absorber:** double/triple‑cation lead iodide with a little Br — `FAMAPbBrI`, `CsFAMAPbBrI`, `FAMAPbI` — i.e. compositions with suppressed δ‑phase, wide grains and ~1.55–1.6 eV gap. Sn‑, Bi‑, Sb‑, Ge‑containing and pure‑Br/Cs‑only absorbers are all capped far lower (Sn²⁺ oxidation → p‑doping and bulk SRH; wide‑gap CsPbBr loses Jsc).
- **n‑i‑p side:** compact/np **SnO₂** or **TiO₂‑c|TiO₂‑mp** with a *thin passivating interlayer* (KCl, SnO₂ overlayer, thiourea, C60/PCBM SAM, amine‑acid) — these consistently sit 19–21 %, because the ETL/perovskite interface is where the Voc deficit of nip cells comes from.
- **HTL:** doped **Spiro‑MeOTAD**, and especially Spiro with an inserted passivant (SrCl₂, CH₃O‑PEIA, HS‑Ph‑CN, OAI) or a better‑matched spiro‑type dopant‑free HTM. The single best training row (22.91 %) is `FAMAPbBrI | OAPbI` with **DM** as HTL — DM (a spiro‑type/fluorene‑based HTM) with a 2D OAI capping gave record Voc.
- **p‑i‑n side:** the winners are **PTAA / SAM (2PACz) + C60|BCP + Cu/Ag** (18.1–20.3 %); PEDOT:PSS as HTL caps ~15 % because of its low WF and non‑selective, acidic interface. A **PFN‑Br / PFN‑P2 dipole layer on PTAA** further improves hole extraction and wetting.
- **Back contact:** Au (nip) or Cu/Ag with C60|BCP (pin); carbon and Al drop performance.

**Screening the pool with this:** discard everything Sn/Bi/Sb‑based (c016, c046, c053, c054, c068, c072, c075, c076, c078, c096, c020, c004…), all PEDOT:PSS‑HTL pin cells (c003, c009, c011, c023, c040, c042, c050, c056, c073, c081, c095), carbon/HTL‑free mesoscopic stacks (c022, c035, c066, c067, c082, c094), wide‑gap CsPbBr/CsPbI‑only and exotic ETLs (c037, c052, c074, c077, c088), and flexible substrates (c043, c095, c097).

**Best remaining recipes:**
- **c019** – FAMAPbBrI / TiO2‑c|mp / **DM** / Au: the exact HTM of the top training device on the canonical mesoporous triple‑layer; deep HOMO match and low interfacial recombination → highest expected PCE.
- **c085** – CsFAMAPbBrI pin / C60|BCP / **PTAA + PFN‑Br** / Cu: the best inverted family in the training set (18.2–20.1 %) plus a dipole interlayer that raises WF and improves PTAA wetting.
- **c061** – CsFAPbI nip / **SnO₂‑c + C60‑SAM** / Spiro / Au: fullerene‑SAM passivation of the SnO₂ interface is precisely the motif that pushes SnO₂ cells above 20 %.
- **c079** – FAMAPbBrI / SnO₂‑np / **CsPbBr₃‑np + Spiro** / Au: perovskite‑nanocrystal interlayer gives graded band alignment and grain‑boundary passivation on the best ETL.
- **c015** – CsFAMAPbBrI capped with **(EPA)PbI 2D layer** / TiO₂ mesoporous / Spiro / Au: 2D capping suppresses surface recombination (same strategy as the 22.9 % record).

Close runners‑up: c093, c047, c008, c059, c071.

**Final: c019, c085, c061, c079, c015**
